media.title: André de Badet — portrait, Gaîté-Lyrique programme, 1941
media.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of André de Badet in jacket and tie, facing the camera.
media.publicCaption: André de Badet, the librettist and lyricist who wrote French words for seven Kaper songs, in the author's portrait printed in the programme of his operetta L'Auberge qui chante at the Gaîté-Lyrique.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified, blindstamp partly legible as “…e STUDIO”; programme of L'Auberge qui chante, Gaîté-Lyrique, 4 October 1941. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Arts du spectacle, 8-RSUPP-879.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not fully cleared. The Wikimedia Commons copy of this Bibliothèque nationale de France scan carries the PD-France tag, but that tag was applied in bulk by an upload bot across the whole digitised volume, no photographer is named on the file page, and the print itself bears a studio blindstamp that is only partly legible. PD-France covers the French term for an anonymous work, seventy years from the 1941 publication, and does not settle United States status: an anonymous French work published in 1941 was still protected in France on the URAA date, so United States copyright was restored and runs ninety-five years from publication. A reduced-resolution crop (500 × 744 px) of a page scanned at 2192 × 2944 px is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
